newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 21.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Winnie Johnson, the mother of one of the Moors Murder victims, has bitterly attacked a High Court judgement allowing Myra Hindley to challenge the decision that she should stay in prison for the rest of her life. Fred Broughton, chairman of the Police Federation, said: "There are certain categories of murder where life should mean life".
IT'S 10 PERCENT OFF IN THE NORWICH SHARE-OUT

The insurance giant Norwich Union is offering 3 million members the chance to buy more shares in the company, due to float in June, at a discount of about 10 percent. Following advice from bankers, the Norwich now believes its shares will be worth between 240p and 290p each, compared to estimates in March of between 220p and 265p.
BRITISH MIDLAND UP 45 PERCENT ON ROUTES LIFT
British Midland saw its profits leap 45 percent last year, following an upgrading of its British business class flights, and the securing of new routes out of Heathrow and into Europe.
Sterling was up sharply against the dollar today, following yesterday's unexpected decision by the US Federal Reserve not to raise US base rates from 5.5 percent.
HK UNDERGROUND TO RAISE 800 MLN STG

The Mass Transit Railway Corporation (MTRC), Hong Kong's equivalent of the London Underground, will be tapping overseas capital markets later this year or early next year, to raise up to 800m stg to spend on refurbishing its network. The MTRC's previous issue was extremely successful, and with even the Labour Government accepting the need for some private sector involvement in the Underground, planners might want to take note of the MTRC's success.
